subject: Request: SLO billing adjustment & temporary grace period after sustained latency
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acmecorp.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Platform Ops <platform-ops@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Persistent latency spikes last week — request for remediation and billing relief

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the on-call review this morning. To summarize our side: between 2026-10-28 14:00 UTC and 2026-10-30 04:00 UTC we saw sustained 99th-percentile token latencies in the 1.8–2.5s range for our production chat route. That materially impacted response times in our customer-facing application (multiple pages of users reported slow responses and some manual retries).

We appreciate the incident report you sent; the attached usage snapshot shows the request patterns on our side. Can Redwood consider a one-off billing relief while you continue the follow-up remediation (we're still waiting on the root-cause post-mortem timeline)? Ideally this would be either:

- a pro-rated credit for the two impacted days, or
- a temporary two-week grace period on overage charges if remediation takes longer.

Our procurement team needs an estimate we can show leadership this week — can you confirm what form of concession Redwood would be willing to offer and how you calculate it?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lim
Director, Platform Reliability
Acme Corp

Attachment: usage_snapshot_10-31-to-11-06.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Persistent latency spikes last week — request for remediation and billing relief

Hi Sarah —

Really sorry for the disruption and thank you for the clear summary and the usage snapshot. We take production latency SLOs seriously and I want to get you a concrete proposal quickly. Quick answers:

- We're preparing a technical post-mortem and a mitigation timeline (will share v1 by 2026-11-05).
- For commercial relief, we can offer either a pro-rated credit for the impacted window or a time-limited grace on overages; I need approval from our commercial ops/finance team for the exact numbers.

Requesting a short sign-off from our side so we can give Acme something to present to procurement today. Can Karthik and Marissa weigh in on a recommended structure (percentage credit vs. grace period)?

I'll attach the incident report we're compiling and the rough token counts for the window in a follow-up.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident_report_20261101.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Persistent latency spikes last week — request for remediation and billing relief

Looping in finance ops context. High level proposal options for Acme (to decide quickly):

Option A — Pro-rated credit:
- Credit equal to the gross usage charges during the incident window (2 days) capped at 25% of monthly invoice.
- Rationale: immediate accounting-friendly credit, easy to apply.

Option B — Temporary grace period on overage + technical support:
- Two-week grace on overage charges for the Acme production route (no overage billing during the window), plus a single technical deep-dive session.
- Rationale: better for short-term stabilization and customer sentiment.

Option C — Hybrid:
- Smaller pro-rated credit (10% of monthly invoice) + one free week of dedicated tuning support and a follow-up SLO review.

Prefer Option B for customer retention unless finance needs a clean credit line. Please advise if we should escalate to Jonas for exec sign-off (this would be >$75k concession).

—Karthik
VP, Commercial Operations
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Persistent latency spikes last week — request for remediation and billing relief

Thanks for the context. I recommend we lead with Option B but quantify the expected cost before promising. Preliminary numbers from billing: 2 impacted days ~ $18,700 gross usage; typical monthly invoice is ~$420k. If we do a two-week overage grace that prevents $0–$25k in overage collection, the expected revenue impact is modest vs. the retention risk.

Suggested commercial phrasing for approval: 
- Provide Acme a two-week overage grace for their production route starting 2026-11-01 through 2026-11-14.
- Apply a pro-rated goodwill credit equal to 15% of the gross charges for the two impacted days (approx $2,800) to show acknowledgement of customer impact.
- Include one complimentary 90-minute technical review with a senior SRE to walk through mitigations and recommended config changes.

Ask: Jonas, can you approve this hybrid package (est. $21k gross impact) as a one-off concession under the customer success discretionary budget? If yes, we'll issue the credit and the grace and schedule the SRE session.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Enterprise Accounts
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T15:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Persistent latency spikes last week — request for remediation and billing relief

Approved.

Jonas Weber (for exec sign-off) — I approve the hybrid concession as outlined by Marissa: two-week overage grace (2026-11-01 through 2026-11-14), a pro-rated goodwill credit = 15% of the two impacted days (apply to next invoice), and a 90-minute SRE session to be scheduled within 10 business days. Charge to Customer Success discretionary — code CS-DISCRETIONARY-2026.

Neha: please confirm messaging to Acme and copy legal/finance when you issue the credit so billing can reconcile.

Thanks,
Jonas
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference
